December 5, 2024

![Illustration of 2024 in pixelated font and a smiling 0](data:image/png;base64,)![Illustration of 2024 in pixelated font and a smiling 0](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/d586522c39ede9792312e60c3239cb68d5c78a21-994x532.png?w=1632&h=873&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)

Every update in Figma is created in dialogue with our community—how you work and what you create pushes us to make Figma better for you.

The numbers tell part of the story: **180 [new releases](https://www.figma.com/blog/figma-2024-we-shipped-it-you-shaped-it/)**

**, 10,000 [Config](https://config.figma.com/) attendees, and over 220 [Friends of Figma](https://friends.figma.com/) groups worldwide.** But the bigger story is how you brought our tools to life. In other words—we ship it, you shape it. To close out the year, let’s take a look at what we built, together.

[![A bird carries a pixelated envelope in its beak.](data:image/png;base64,)![A bird carries a pixelated envelope in its beak.](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/4a18a0454dc6ef7abea9e44a1db643e0146a50db-2160x1216.png?w=2160&h=1216&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)](https://www.figma.com/blog/newsletter/)

Want the next issue delivered straight to your inbox? [Sign up here](https://www.figma.com/blog/newsletter/).

## [Pushing our products further](#pushing-our-products-further)

From major launches to much-anticipated updates, the real design process starts when you get your hands on new features. We refined UI3 to give you more control, reworked AI tools with intention, enhanced Dev Mode for smoother code-to-design connections, and launched Figma Slides to give your work the stage it deserves.

[![Colorful illustration of 2024 in pixelated font with a smiley face on top of 4](data:image/png;base64,)![Colorful illustration of 2024 in pixelated font with a smiley face on top of 4](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/013773abfba8ec4f95e5ef994fe866395f6bbb58-1260x730.png?w=528&h=306&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)](https://www.figma.com/blog/figma-2024-we-shipped-it-you-shaped-it/)

## [Going big for Config](#going-big-for-config)

This year’s Config was our biggest yet, bringing together over 10,000 attendees in San Francisco to explore the future of building products. With early bird tickets on sale for [Config 2025](https://config.figma.com/), we’re sharing the talks that rocked the house.

[![A tableau of clay objects: a baseball cap reading “Enya,” a daisy, a tomato, a Wordle grid, and a pixelated letter A](data:image/png;base64,)![A tableau of clay objects: a baseball cap reading “Enya,” a daisy, a tomato, a Wordle grid, and a pixelated letter A](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/e8af1cc25b245a54ba0fa2f13ec662c742a5d26f-1260x730.png?w=528&h=306&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)](https://www.figma.com/blog/8-ways-to-craft-an-unforgettable-config-talk/)

[**Read more**](https://www.figma.com/blog/8-ways-to-craft-an-unforgettable-config-talk/)

## [New tools, new look](#new-tools-new-look)

As we expanded our toolkit for developers, marketers, and entire product teams, we knew that our brand needed to change, too. This year, we revamped our visual identity, introduced a new typeface, and—as Brand Designer Becca Ramos dives into here—used our own tools to overhaul our web system.

[![Examples of Figma’s web system including variables, “Get started” buttons, colors, and display and title type.](data:image/png;base64,)![Examples of Figma’s web system including variables, “Get started” buttons, colors, and display and title type.](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/07e8e0b7788e93735ea8ed9a96cbbdd89352f301-1260x730.png?w=528&h=306&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)](https://www.figma.com/blog/updating-our-web-system-for-a-new-era/)

## [Rabbit hole](#rabbit-hole)

![A collage shows (1) a medieval scroll, (2) an illustration of a man with curly hair, and (3) an abstract graphic showing an annotation on a bubbly shape.](data:image/png;base64,)![A collage shows (1) a medieval scroll, (2) an illustration of a man with curly hair, and (3) an abstract graphic showing an annotation on a bubbly shape.](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/8e3ad36d50c931961b548f0db492b594be12ea0b-1300x730.png?rect=0,1,1300,729&w=804&h=451&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)

1\. For presentations that pack a punch, we’re turning to [these community templates for Figma Slides](https://www.figma.com/blog/figma-2024-we-shipped-it-you-shaped-it/#introducing-figma-slides).

2\. Delighting your users starts with delighting yourself, says Pablo Sánchez. The designer of Ableton’s Note app shares [7 rules for designing the unexpected](https://www.figma.com/blog/pablo-sanchezs-7-rules-for-designing-the-unexpected/)

.

3\. Developers are designers, too. One North’s Nick Villapiano explains why devs should [play an active role in the design process](https://www.figma.com/blog/why-devs-should-play-an-active-role-in-design/)

.
